title: Name every wagon verb-object

facts.note: Planner task mentions a wagon or its slug/name.
Needs a plan observer that enumerates wagon slugs in the plan being confirmed (subject_kind: wagon); telling introduced/renamed slugs apart additionally needs plan history or a diff.
Validator runs at CONFIRM and blocks confirmation; phase must be reported by the harness.
naming_pattern validator finding carrying wagon_slug and reason; needs a validator-finding observer.

fires: Planner introduces a new wagon whose slug will be confirmed
CONFIRM runs over a plan containing any wagon with a single-token, noun-first, non-kebab-case or connective-bearing slug
doesNotFire: Naming of artifacts that are not wagons (features, WMBTs, acceptances) — other naming conventions cover those

given: A plan contains a wagon slug that will pass through CONFIRM
when: The planner chooses or keeps the wagon slug (checked at CONFIRM, confirm-blocking)
then: The wagon slug is verb-object: kebab-case, at least two tokens, the leading token a verb from the convention verb lexicon, and no connective tokens.
prefer: Lead with an action verb from the verb lexicon at conventions:planner:feature#/artifact_seeds/verb_selection, then the object it acts on (e.g. resolve-dilemmas, manage-users, route-request, preview-changes, respond-event)
When a wagon slug is a brand or proper-noun name, list it explicitly in wagon.convention.yaml verb_object_enforcement.brand_exceptions
avoid: Noun-first or object-verb slugs such as mode-select
Connective tokens in the slug (e.g. and/or/of-style joiners)
Treating a brand or proper-noun slug as implicitly exempt — an unlisted exception is a violation
Adding an ordinary (non-brand, non-proper-noun) slug to brand_exceptions to bypass the rule
unless: The slug is a brand or proper-noun name listed explicitly in wagon.convention.yaml verb_object_enforcement.brand_exceptions
why: A verb-object slug states what the wagon does, keeping wagon names uniform and aligned with the shared verb lexicon; explicit brand exceptions keep deviations visible and reviewable.
evidence: CONFIRM completes without a planner_wagon_name_is_verb_object finding for any wagon in the plan
Any failure reports wagon_slug and reason
Every non-verb-object slug in the plan is a brand or proper-noun name and is listed explicitly in wagon.convention.yaml verb_object_enforcement.brand_exceptions
verifier_detail: validation: family=format, template=naming_pattern, variant=planner_wagon_name_is_verb_object, phase=CONFIRM, enforcement=confirm-blocking, subject_kind=wagon

Checks: kebab-case; token count >= 2; leading token in verb lexicon; no connective tokens; a slug failing these passes only if it is a brand or proper-noun name explicitly listed in verb_object_enforcement.brand_exceptions (implicit exceptions are violations)
Term wagon_verb_object: 'the verb-object naming rule for a wagon slug'
examples_ok: resolve-dilemmas, manage-users, route-request, preview-changes, respond-event
Implementation: validator, ref test_wagon_name_is_verb_object::test_confirm_blocks_non_verb_object_wagon (confirm-blocking test of the detector)

additions.justification: Explains why the source's bad examples fail, derived directly from the statement's checks; adds no new obligation.

additions.justification: Restates the source's restriction that only brand or proper-noun slugs are eligible exceptions; prevents metric gaming. No new obligation.
